_about: Provenance for the knowledge base. Two ingestion streams, tagged by `stream`: (1) CRAFT-INSTRUCTION — the centuries-long body of writing tutorials, poetics, and craft manuals, the source of abstract heuristics; (2) FICTION-CORPUS — public-domain stories for pattern analysis; plus (3) REFERENCE works. Titles, authors, and dates are facts (not copyrightable). We extract abstract craft features (claims, heuristics, failure modes) and NEVER reproduce protected text. `license`/`copyright_note` record what may be copied and flag the German/EU check: US public-domain status does NOT settle EU/DE status (EU term is life + 70 years).

sources.title: Poetics
sources.creator: Aristotle
sources.location: c. 335 BCE; use a public-domain translation (e.g. Butcher, 1895)
sources.notes: Foundational: unity of action, complication/unraveling, peripeteia (reversal), anagnorisis (recognition), hamartia. Extract structure heuristics.
sources.copyright_note: Original PD worldwide. Modern translations may be in copyright; prefer a PD translation.

sources.title: Ars Poetica
sources.creator: Horace
sources.notes: Decorum, character consistency, in medias res, 'labor of the file' (revision). Abstract maxims only.
sources.copyright_note: Original PD worldwide; use a PD translation.

sources.title: On the Sublime
sources.creator: Longinus (attrib.)
sources.notes: Sources of elevated writing: great conception, strong emotion, figures, diction, arrangement. Extract as abstract effect-levers.
sources.copyright_note: Original PD; use a PD translation.

sources.title: Die Technik des Dramas (Technique of the Drama)
sources.creator: Gustav Freytag
sources.notes: The five-part dramatic arc ('Freytag's pyramid'). Note it describes classical TRAGEDY; do not apply mechanically to all forms. German-language primary source.
sources.copyright_note: PD in the EU and DE (Freytag d. 1895, well past life+70) and in the US. Fully clear for ingestion.

sources.title: The Philosophy of Composition (and critical reviews)
sources.creator: Edgar Allan Poe
sources.notes: Single preconceived effect; every element subordinate to it; compose backward from the intended close. Abstract heuristics.

sources.title: The Art of Fiction (essay) and Prefaces to the New York Edition
sources.creator: Henry James
sources.notes: Dramatize; the 'scenic method'; the central-consciousness / reflector; 'render, don't report'. Extract as abstract craft.
sources.copyright_note: PD worldwide (James d. 1916; EU term expired 1986).

sources.title: The Craft of Fiction
sources.creator: Percy Lubbock
sources.notes: Systematizes James: 'picture' (summary/telling) vs 'drama' (scene/showing); the governing point of view. Abstract features only.
sources.copyright_note: US public domain (pub. 1921). EU/DE: Lubbock d. 1965, so protected until 2035-12-31 — do NOT ingest full text in the EU; paraphrase abstract concepts only.

sources.title: Aspects of the Novel
sources.creator: E. M. Forster
sources.notes: 'The king died and then the queen died' (story) vs 'died of grief' (plot = causality); flat vs round characters; pattern and rhythm. Abstract features.
sources.copyright_note: US public domain (pub. 1927, entered PD 2023). EU/DE: Forster d. 1970, protected until 2040-12-31 — paraphrase concepts only, no full-text ingestion in the EU.

sources.title: The Elements of Style (Strunk, 1918 edition)
sources.creator: William Strunk Jr.
sources.notes: 'Omit needless words'; positive statement; active voice. The original Strunk edition; the later White revisions are separate and in copyright.
sources.copyright_note: 1918 Strunk-only edition is PD in the US and (Strunk d. 1946) now PD in the EU/DE. White-revised editions remain in copyright.

sources.title: The Living Handbook of Narratology
sources.creator: Hamburg University (eds.)
sources.notes: Concept definitions (focalization, order/duration/frequency, eventfulness/tellability). Summarize; do not paste article text.

sources.title: The Art of Dramatic Writing
sources.creator: Lajos Egri
sources.notes: Premise as testable proposition; character contradiction; orchestration of forces. No text reproduction.
sources.copyright_note: US: possibly PD via non-renewal (verify). DE/EU: Egri d. 1967, protected until 2037. Treat as in-copyright in the EU; abstract features only.

sources.title: Techniques of the Selling Writer
sources.creator: Dwight V. Swain
sources.notes: Scene/sequel structure and motivation-reaction units as abstract patterns.
sources.copyright_note: In-copyright (Swain d. 1992; EU until 2062). Abstract features only.

sources.title: Dialogue: The Art of Verbal Action
sources.creator: Robert McKee
sources.notes: Dialogue as action with objective/subtext/turn. No text reproduction.

sources.title: How Fiction Works
sources.creator: James Wood
sources.notes: Free indirect discourse and the mechanics of narrative distance as abstract craft.

sources.title: The Art of Fiction
sources.creator: John Gardner
sources.notes: 'Continuous dream' and psychic-distance gradations as abstract concepts.
sources.copyright_note: In-copyright (Gardner d. 1982; EU until 2052). Abstract features only.

sources.title: Reading Like a Writer
sources.creator: Francine Prose
sources.notes: Close-reading discipline and specificity heuristics. No text reproduction.

sources.title: Contemporary online writing tutorials, craft essays, and workshop lore
sources.creator: various (blogs, MFA handouts, craft sites, author essays)
sources.location: the open web (individually cite when a specific heuristic is drawn from one)
sources.notes: The large modern body of writing instruction. Mine for ABSTRACT heuristics and failure modes; cite the specific source per heuristic; never paste passages. Cross-check any single claim against the classical sources before promoting it to a card (do not learn a rule from one blog post).
sources.copyright_note: Mixed/in-copyright. Abstract features only; attribute per heuristic.

sources.title: Standard Ebooks (public-domain corpus)
sources.creator: Standard Ebooks
sources.notes: US-public-domain texts for corpus analysis (annotation and abstract feature extraction, not wholesale reproduction into prompts).
sources.copyright_note: US public domain. EU/DE status must be verified per author death date before ingesting any specific title.

sources.title: Project Gutenberg (public-domain corpus)
sources.creator: Project Gutenberg
sources.notes: Large PD text corpus for pattern analysis. Licensing is US-centric.
sources.copyright_note: Status determined by US copyright. From Germany, verify EU/DE status (author death + 70) per title before ingesting.
